story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_fellhammer.o1.t: Find the bell of the drowned temple
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_fellhammer.o2.r: Three strokes, slow, the way they rang it for the dead. I'll hang it on the cliff where the temple stood. Let the sea hear it ring from this side for once.
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_fellhammer.o2.t: Bring the bell to Ysolde Frost-Hand in Winterhold
The bell from the drowned temple.
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_fellhammer.outr: On the lowest tide of Evening Star, Ysolde rings the bell three times. Some swear they hear an answer from beneath the water.
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_fellhammer.pitc: There's a fence at Fort Fellhammer selling a bell they say came up from the drowned temple. Ysolde Frost-Hand's been asking every trader in the hold about it.
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_frostmoth.desc: Aulus Vettrius's brother Gaius went into Fort Frostmoth to recover the cohort standard of their great-grandfather's legion. The fort's dead still stand to at their posts, and Gaius has not returned.
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_frostmoth.o0.te: Lay the restless legionaries of Fort Frostmoth to rest
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_frostmoth.o1.jo: Gaius Vettrius lay by the inner hall, dead of his wounds, his hand still reaching for the standard.
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_frostmoth.o1.te: Relieve the officer's shade of his command
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_frostmoth.o2.te: Take the cohort standard from the inner hall
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_frostmoth.o3.re: ...He got further than anyone in two hundred years. That's a Vettrius for you. I'll hang the standard over my door, and I'll take the next ship to bring Gaius home. The cohort's dismissed. They've earned it.
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_frostmoth.o3.te: Bring the standard to Aulus Vettrius in Raven Rock
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_frostmoth.o3.to: The standard. And I'm sorry: Gaius didn't make it out.
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_frostmoth.offer: You look like a man with a weight on him.
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_frostmoth.outro: Aulus has hung the cohort's standard over his door in Raven Rock. The Redoran Guard pretend not to see it. Some of them salute it anyway.
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_frostmoth.pitch: My brother Gaius went into Fort Frostmoth to bring our great-grandfather's cohort standard home. The dead there are still standing to, two hundred years after the mountain burst. Gaius hasn't come back. Bring the standard, and if you can, give those poor soldiers their orders to stand down.
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_frostmoth.title: Stand Down
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_greenwall.desc: The bandits at Fort Greenwall charge every cart a toll except the Black-Briars'. Their chief, Brannoc Tollhand, keeps a book of every coin. Somebody in Riften would very much like it to burn.
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_greenwall.o0.jo: Brannoc Tollhand died with his strongbox key around his neck.
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_greenwall.o0.te: Break the Greenwall toll gang and its chief
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_greenwall.o1.te: Take the toll book from Brannoc's strongbox
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_greenwall.o2.c0: Put it before the Jarl. Let Riften see who it pays.
Then I'll read it aloud in court myself, and see who goes pale. Maven will know it was us. Watch your back on the canal.
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_greenwall.o2.c1: Burn it. Nobody in this hold will act on it anyway.
Wise, maybe. Cowardly, maybe. Both, probably. I'll fetch a candle. And I'll remember that the road is quieter now, at least.
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_greenwall.o2.re: Shor's bones. Every Briar wagon, every bribe, every guard who looked away. What do you want done with it?
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_greenwall.o2.te: Decide what becomes of the toll book
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_greenwall.outro: Brannoc Tollhand will charge no more tolls on the Riften road. What became of his book is between me, a clerk named Ingrith and, sooner or later, Maven Black-Briar.
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_greenwall.pitch: You want to know who really runs the Riften road? Brannoc Tollhand at Fort Greenwall keeps a book. Get the book and you'll know. Then you'll wish you didn't.
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_greenwall.title: The Toll Book
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_greymoor.desc: The last paymaster of Fort Greymoor buried the garrison's back pay outside the walls, thirty paces from the south-west tower, under a stone marked with the Legion eagle. He never returned for it.
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_greymoor.o0.jou: The eagle stone was half sunk in the turf. Beneath it lay the pay chest, rusted but whole, and inside it the garrison's silver ring of service.
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_greymoor.o0.tex: Dig under the eagle stone south-west of the fort
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_greymoor.outro: Optio Gratian Sabe wanted the pay to go to whoever served the Empire best. I suppose I'll have to decide whether that's me.
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_greymoor.pitch: Old soldiers swear the Legion buried two months' pay outside Fort Greymoor when they pulled out. Under a stone with the eagle on it, south-west of the fort. Mind the Silver Hand on the walls.
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_greymoor.title: The Buried Pay
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_kastav.desc: Grelka Iron-Jaw, the bandit chief of Fort Kastav, is bleeding Anga's Mill dry with her timber tribute. Hallvard at the mill would pay to see it stopped.
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_kastav.o1.journ: Grelka is dead. The self-styled Lady of Kastav will collect no more tolls.
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_kastav.o1.text: Put an end to Grelka Iron-Jaw
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_kastav.o2.reply: No more tribute? Then this winter we patch our own roofs first. Here, it's not much, but it's honest timber money.
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_kastav.o2.topic: Grelka won't be collecting any more planks.
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_kastav.outro: Anga's Mill sends its timber to Windhelm again, and for once the planks stay on the right side of the road.
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_kastav.pitch: The Kastav bandits take half of what Anga's Mill cuts. Hallvard says he'd give his saw to see Grelka gone. Well, not his saw. But something.
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_kastav.title: Twenty Planks a Week
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_neugrad.desc: Captain Ulfgar Broadshield and his deserters hold Fort Neugrad and the Legion's payroll coffer, which lies under the third flagstone from the cellar stair.
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_neugrad.o2.jour: Broadshield's key opened the coffer under the third flagstone. The Legion's eight hundred septims are all there.
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_neugrad.o3.c0.l: Return it to the Legion through the hold.
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_neugrad.o3.c0.r: Honest. I'll see it goes west to the camp under guard, and I'll see your name goes with it.
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_neugrad.o3.c1.l: I'm keeping it. They abandoned it.
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_neugrad.o3.c1.r: I didn't hear that. I didn't see the coffer. Get it out of my sight before I remember I'm a bailiff.
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_neugrad.o3.repl: Eight hundred septims of Legion silver. The Legion will want it back. The Stormcloaks would find it very useful. And you, I imagine, could find a use for it too.
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_neugrad.o3.text: Decide what to do with the payroll
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_neugrad.o3.topi: I've recovered the Legion's payroll from Fort Neugrad.
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_neugrad.outro: A prisoner named Pell walks out of Fort Neugrad's cells into daylight for the first time in weeks, blinking.
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_neugrad.pitch: When the Legion left Fort Neugrad, Captain Broadshield stayed behind with the garrison's payroll. Eight hundred septims. He calls his men the Free Company now. I call them thieves with good boots.
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_neugrad.title: The Payroll Never Arrived
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_snowhawk.desc: Thorvar Mist-Eye, steward of Highmoon Hall, sent three guards to investigate Fort Snowhawk. None returned.
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_snowhawk.o0.tex: Put down the marsh dead in Fort Snowhawk
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_snowhawk.o1.jou: Vigdis is dead. Her journal names all three guards. Hallgerd's charcoal note was hidden in the cage.
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_snowhawk.o2.rep: ...Hallgerd wrote that it wasn't my fault. That's like her. I'll read it to her mother myself. And then I'll burn this book, and then I'll have a drink, and then I'll be steward again.
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_snowhawk.o2.tex: Bring Vigdis's journal to Thorvar in Morthal
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_snowhawk.o2.top: Your patrol is dead. Here's the one who did it, in her own words.
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_snowhawk.offer: Has something happened to your patrol?
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_snowhawk.outro: Three pyres burn outside Morthal's walls. Jarl Idgrod stands at the window of Highmoon Hall the whole night, watching them.
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_snowhawk.pitch: Three of the Jarl's guards went to look at the smoke over Fort Snowhawk. Sten, Ofrid and Hallgerd. Hallgerd's mother asks me every morning. I sent them, so it's mine to answer. Find them. If the worst has happened, find who did it.
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_snowhawk.title: The Missing Patrol
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_sungard.desc: Vatrius Hollow, a Legion deserter, holds Fort Sungard with a band of turncoats, taxing the road in the Emperor's name. As long as the cohort's eagle standard hangs in his hall, his men believe they are still soldiers.
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_sungard.o1.text: Break the deserters on the walls
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_sungard.o3.jour: The eagle standard came off its hooks easily. Without it, Fort Sungard is just an empty fort full of tired men.
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_sungard.outro: The road past Fort Sungard is free again. Somewhere in the Legion's records, the Fourth Cohort's eagle is still listed as lost.
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_sungard.pitch: Fort Sungard's 'garrison' charged my brother thirty septims to use his own road. They're deserters flying a Legion flag. Take the flag away and I reckon they'll stop pretending.
story.skycraft.q.pl_fort_sungard.title: A Garrison of None
story.skycraft.q.pl_four_skull_lookout.d: Sweet-Tongue Ottar sold fake treasure maps to Four Skull Lookout. His own notes admit the story behind them might be true: a Legion pay chest buried beneath the skull facing west.
story.skycraft.q.pl_four_skull_lookout.o: Under the west skull lay a Legion pay chest from 4E 176, its officer's sword still wrapped in oiled leather. The lie was true all along.
Dig beneath the skull that faces the sunset
Somewhere in Bruma, a paymaster's widow will never know the chest was found. The Emperor will never know either.
story.skycraft.q.pl_four_skull_lookout.p: Everybody laughs at Ottar's maps. But nobody I know ever dug under the west skull at Four Skull Lookout. Everybody gave up before then.
story.skycraft.q.pl_frossel.desc: Brenna Ice-Mead of Thirsk Mead Hall wants the hall's heirloom spear back from Kruk Gnaw-Tooth, the riekling chief of Frossel. Her hunter Gunnar advises going at dusk, and going loud.
story.skycraft.q.pl_frossel.o0.text: Find the riekling den at Frossel
story.skycraft.q.pl_frossel.o3.reply: Then carve the name on the beam, and somebody fetch the good mead. The spear is yours, as I swore. Bring it to the hall on feast days, or I'll come and get it myself.
story.skycraft.q.pl_frossel.o3.text: Tell Brenna Ice-Mead the spear is won
story.skycraft.q.pl_frossel.o3.topic: Kruk Gnaw-Tooth is dead, and the Spear of Thirsk is free.
story.skycraft.q.pl_frossel.outro: Your name is cut into the beam of Thirsk Mead Hall below the chieftains'. The rieklings of Frossel, Brenna says, have started telling a story about you too.
story.skycraft.q.pl_frossel.pitch: The riekling chief Kruk Gnaw-Tooth carried it off to Frossel when his folk held our hall. We took the hall back with axes. The spear's still in his fists. Go at dusk, go loud, and bring it home. Swear to bring it to the hall on feast days, and you can keep it.
story.skycraft.q.pl_frossel.title: The Spear of Thirsk
story.skycraft.q.pl_frostflow_lighthouse: The keeper of Frostflow Lighthouse followed something that stole his lens down into the tunnels beneath the tower. The light has been dark for nine nights.
Clear the tunnels beneath the lighthouse
The Falmer had set the lens up in their den like an idol. Keeper Eirik's axe lay beside it.
The Frostflow light burns again over the Sea of Ghosts.
Set the lens back in the lamp
Captain Hjolfrid's ship passes the point safely that night. She does not write a thank-you letter. She does not burn your furniture either.
Frostflow Lighthouse has gone dark and the keeper's gone missing. A ship nearly broke on the point last week. Somebody needs to get that lamp burning.
story.skycraft.q.pl_frostmere_crypt.desc: Grave-robbers in Frostmere Crypt stole a wedding band from the fresh grave of Gerdir, wife of Sigvald. Their chief, Kjeld the Gravewolf, refuses to sell it back.
story.skycraft.q.pl_frostmere_crypt.o2.j: Under the cairn lay forty septims and a note: 'For whoever is kinder than the last.' You leave the ring and take the coin.
story.skycraft.q.pl_frostmere_crypt.o2.t: Leave the ring at the cairn on the crypt road for Sigvald
story.skycraft.q.pl_frostmere_crypt.outr: Gerdir's grave is closed again. Sigvald wears her ring on a cord around his neck.
story.skycraft.q.pl_frostmere_crypt.pitc: The robbers in Frostmere Crypt took old Sigvald's dead wife's ring right off her finger. He's been leaving them notes. They've been laughing.
story.skycraft.q.pl_frostmoon_crag.desc: Sigvar, the hunter of the Abandoned Lodge, followed a white wolf to Frostmoon Crag and joined the pack. He wears his wife Helga's ring on a thong around his throat. She is still waiting for him in Raven Rock.
story.skycraft.q.pl_frostmoon_crag.o0.te: Find the pack at Frostmoon Crag
story.skycraft.q.pl_frostmoon_crag.o1.te: Face the pack's leader, the Grey Brother
story.skycraft.q.pl_frostmoon_crag.o2.jo: The Grey Brother wore a silver ring on a chewed thong. Inside it is engraved: To S., from H., for every Loredas.
story.skycraft.q.pl_frostmoon_crag.o2.te: Take the ring from the Grey Brother's throat
story.skycraft.q.pl_frostmoon_crag.o3.re: He kept it. All that time, whatever he was, he kept it. ...Then I can stop climbing that hill. Thank you. I think. Leave me a while.
story.skycraft.q.pl_frostmoon_crag.o3.te: Bring the ring to Helga in Raven Rock
story.skycraft.q.pl_frostmoon_crag.outro: Helga no longer goes to the lodge on Loredas. She goes to the shrine instead, and lights a candle, and comes home before dark.
story.skycraft.q.pl_frostmoon_crag.pitch: The hunter from the Abandoned Lodge went chasing a white wolf to Frostmoon Crag. His wife Helga goes up to the lodge every Loredas. Somebody should find out what became of him, for her sake.
story.skycraft.q.pl_frostmoon_crag.title: Every Loredas
story.skycraft.q.pl_gallows_rock.desc: Werewolf hunters dragged the sawyer Ulmir from Mixwater Mill to the old fort at Gallows Rock. His brother Torvar wants him freed.
story.skycraft.q.pl_gallows_rock.o0.text: Break the hunters' hold on Gallows Rock
story.skycraft.q.pl_gallows_rock.o1.jour: The chains were already broken when I reached the cell. The thing inside wore a man's iron ring on one claw. Ulmir's confession lay on the floor in charcoal.
story.skycraft.q.pl_gallows_rock.o1.text: Face what waits in the chains
story.skycraft.q.pl_gallows_rock.o2.c0.l: Tell him Ulmir was a werewolf, and show him the confession.
story.skycraft.q.pl_gallows_rock.o2.c0.r: Two winters. Two winters of 'deer'. ...He washed his hands in the river every morning and I thought he was just tidy. Give me the ring. I'll bury it under the saw-pit, where he worked. In the daylight.
story.skycraft.q.pl_gallows_rock.o2.c1.l: Tell him the hunters killed Ulmir before you arrived.
story.skycraft.q.pl_gallows_rock.o2.c1.r: Then I'll see every one of them in the ground. ...You've done that already, haven't you? Good. Give me the ring. He was a good man. Whatever they said, he was a good man.
story.skycraft.q.pl_gallows_rock.o2.repl: You've his ring. You wouldn't have his ring if... Tell me straight. I can take it straight.
story.skycraft.q.pl_gallows_rock.o2.text: Tell Torvar at Mixwater Mill what you found
story.skycraft.q.pl_gallows_rock.outro: Torvar has started sleeping with a lamp lit.
story.skycraft.q.pl_gallows_rock.pitch: Torvar at Mixwater Mill has been begging anyone with a blade to go to Gallows Rock. Hunters took his brother in chains. Torvar swears he's innocent. Torvar would.
story.skycraft.q.pl_gallows_rock.title: The Beast of Mixwater
story.skycraft.q.pl_geirmunds_hall.desc: Eydis Long-Net's husband Arne rowed a scholar to Geirmund's Hall and never came back. She asks for the soapstone net-weight he wore.
story.skycraft.q.pl_geirmunds_hall.o0.te: Cross Lake Geir to Geirmund's Hall
story.skycraft.q.pl_geirmunds_hall.o1.jo: Arne and the College scholar lay together near the flooded stair. She had finished her chapter. He had his hand on her shoulder.
story.skycraft.q.pl_geirmunds_hall.o2.re: That's him. That's exactly him. He never could leave anyone in the dark. Thank you. I can stop standing on the dock now.
story.skycraft.q.pl_geirmunds_hall.o2.te: Bring the net-weight to Eydis in Ivarstead
story.skycraft.q.pl_geirmunds_hall.o2.to: Arne didn't leave her alone in there. He stayed with the scholar to the end.
story.skycraft.q.pl_geirmunds_hall.outro: Eydis has stopped waiting on the dock. She wears the soapstone fish around her own neck now.
story.skycraft.q.pl_geirmunds_hall.pitch: My husband Arne. He rowed a College woman out to the island in Lake Geir and the lake gave back the boat, not him. He wore a soapstone fish I carved. If you're going out there, bring it home to me.
story.skycraft.q.pl_geirmunds_hall.title: What the Lake Kept
story.skycraft.q.pl_glacial_cave.desc: Smugglers have seized the Glacial Cave to cut stalhrim without the Skaal's words, and taken the cutting pick from Aevar Stone-Ear's apprentice. The ice has woken something cold in answer.
story.skycraft.q.pl_glacial_cave.o0.text: Drive the stalhrim smugglers out of the Glacial Cave
story.skycraft.q.pl_glacial_cave.o1.jour: Hjalmar, the apprentice, is free and on his way home. He told me the smugglers never learned the words.
story.skycraft.q.pl_glacial_cave.o2.repl: Good. Good. The ice will settle now that the greedy ones are gone. You have done the All-Maker a kindness, which is rarer than you would think.
story.skycraft.q.pl_glacial_cave.o2.text: Return the pick to Aevar Stone-Ear in the Skaal Village
story.skycraft.q.pl_glacial_cave.o2.topi: Your apprentice is free, and here is your pick.
story.skycraft.q.pl_glacial_cave.outro: Aevar has gone to the Glacial Cave to say the words over the broken slabs. He says the ice will forgive the cuts in time. He did not say whether it would forgive the cutters.
story.skycraft.q.pl_glacial_cave.pitch: Aevar Stone-Ear's apprentice went to the Glacial Cave and found smugglers hacking at the stalhrim. They took the pick his master gave him. Aevar wants it back, and wants the cutting stopped.
story.skycraft.q.pl_glacial_cave.title: The Ice Is Crying
story.skycraft.q.pl_gloombound_mine.desc: Mogdurz of Narzulbur wants vengeance for her husband Dushgar, lost in the east drift of Gloombound Mine where the miners broke into something old and blind.
story.skycraft.q.pl_gloombound_mine.o0.t: Clear the east drift of Gloombound Mine
story.skycraft.q.pl_gloombound_mine.o1.t: Kill the creature that took Dushgar
story.skycraft.q.pl_gloombound_mine.o2.j: Dushgar went down fighting; there were three dead Falmer under him. His clan ring was still on his fist.
story.skycraft.q.pl_gloombound_mine.o3.r: Of course he did. Malacath heard me, then, and sent you. ...Take this. Ebony from the drift he opened. He'd want it in an outsider's hand, if the outsider earned it. You earned it.
story.skycraft.q.pl_gloombound_mine.o3.t: Bring Dushgar's ring to Mogdurz in Narzulbur
Dushgar died with his axe in his hand.
story.skycraft.q.pl_gloombound_mine.offe: You look like you're carrying a grudge.
story.skycraft.q.pl_gloombound_mine.outr: The east drift of Gloombound Mine is open again. The miners leave a cup of mead at the crack for Dushgar.
story.skycraft.q.pl_gloombound_mine.pitc: My husband Dushgar went down Gloombound's east drift to prove he wasn't afraid. He was right: he wasn't. Something down there ate him anyway. Bring me what's left, and the head of what did it.
story.skycraft.q.pl_gloomreach.desc: The spore-gatherer Sinnoc went into Gloomreach to harvest glowing fungus for an alchemist in Markarth and never came out. His full satchel is hidden behind the second falls.
story.skycraft.q.pl_gloomreach.o1.text: Find Sinnoc's satchel behind the second falls
story.skycraft.q.pl_gloomreach.o2.journa: The Gardener wore a cord of teeth and one Nord ring. Sinnoc's, I think. The fungus beds will go untended now.
story.skycraft.q.pl_gloomreach.outro: The glowing caps fetch a fine price in Markarth. Sinnoc's debt to his alchemist is paid, as he wanted.
story.skycraft.q.pl_gloomreach.pitch: Fellow called Sinnoc went into Gloomreach for glowing mushrooms. Took a Markarth alchemist's money in advance and didn't come back. Honest sort, for a mushroom man. His satchel's still down there somewhere.
story.skycraft.q.pl_gloomreach.title: The Gardener's Soil
story.skycraft.q.pl_graywinter_watch.des: A troll in Graywinter Watch has been taking hounds, hunters and even a giant's mammoth calf. The hunter Ulfgar says the Jarl's bounty of 100 septims still stands.
The troll is dead. Its den was littered with arrows it had pulled out of itself.
Kill the troll of Graywinter Watch
Recover Ulfgar's bow from the troll's den
story.skycraft.q.pl_graywinter_watch.out: The bounty on the Graywinter troll has been paid. Ulfgar says he'll carve the troll's tally into his bow.
story.skycraft.q.pl_graywinter_watch.pit: There's a troll in Graywinter Watch, east of the river. The Jarl put a bounty on it and the hunters can't collect. Bring fire. Lots of fire.
story.skycraft.q.pl_greenspring_hollow.d: A hunter's journal tells of the spriggan that keeps Greenspring Hollow, and the poachers whose greed has turned it wild. The hunter says it is the men who need killing, not the spriggan.
story.skycraft.q.pl_greenspring_hollow.o: With the poachers gone, the trees of the hollow seemed to breathe out. Something watched me leave and did not follow.
The keeper of Greenspring Hollow has the bargain back: one deer, a word to Kynareth, and no more.
story.skycraft.q.pl_greenspring_hollow.p: Poachers have camped in Greenspring Hollow, leaving deer to rot for the pelts. The hollow's keeper is angry, and the trees close the paths behind you. Drive the poachers out and maybe it'll calm.
story.skycraft.q.pl_greywater_grotto.des: The herb-wife Ragnhild hid her satchel of white cap in Greywater Grotto before a great frostbite spider caught her. The mushrooms are meant for Brynja's sick son at Half-Moon Mill.
Find Ragnhild's satchel in the dry cleft
White cap. Boiled in milk, three days. She told me that a dozen times. Gods keep her. I'll put the pot on now. And I'll pay for her burial; she'd have hated that, so I'll do it twice as grand.
Bring the white cap to Brynja at Half-Moon Mill
Ragnhild gathered these for your boy. She didn't make it out.
story.skycraft.q.pl_greywater_grotto.out: Brynja's boy is up and about by Turdas, complaining about the taste of mushroom milk.
story.skycraft.q.pl_greywater_grotto.pit: Ragnhild the herb-wife went into Greywater Grotto for white cap mushrooms. Brynja's boy at the mill is sick and needs them. Ragnhild hasn't come back.
story.skycraft.q.pl_greywater_grotto.tit: White Cap for a Sick Boy
story.skycraft.q.pl_gyldenhul_barrow.des: Yrsa Seal-Singer's nephew Brandr went into Gyldenhul Barrow alone to prove himself in the old Skaal way, carrying his father's seal-tooth spear.
Brandr is dead. He fell in the warden's hall, with three broken draugr around him and his father's spear still in his hand.
He fell fighting. Three draugr lay broken around him.
Then the old men will talk about him after all. I will cut his name on the stair myself. Give me the spear; it goes to the next hunter who has more sense than he did.
He should never have gone. Tell the young ones the truth: the proving kills.
...Yes. I will tell them that, and I will tell them his name with it, so they remember both. Give me the spear. It will hang over the door, and nobody will take it into that barrow again.
Your face tells me before your mouth does. Tell me how.
story.skycraft.q.pl_gyldenhul_barrow.out: There is a new name on the stair of Gyldenhul Barrow. Yrsa cut it herself, deep enough that the wind will not wear it away for a long time.
story.skycraft.q.pl_gyldenhul_barrow.pit: My nephew Brandr took his father's spear and went into Gyldenhul Barrow to prove himself, though the old proving is long done with. He said not to send anyone who did not want to go. Do you want to go?
story.skycraft.q.pl_haafingar_stormcloak: A Stormcloak soldier, Ragnvald, wrote a letter to his mother Hulda in Dragon Bridge and never sent it. He asked that a friend carry it home.
Find Ragnvald's unsent letter in the Stormcloak camp
From Ragnvald? ...He can see our chimney. The fool can see our chimney and he never once came down. I'll keep this under my pillow. Don't tell him I cried. Tell him I threw it in the fire.
Carry the letter to Hulda in Dragon Bridge
Your son Ragnvald wrote to you. He couldn't send it himself.
That night a lamp burns in Hulda's window until dawn, facing the hills.
There's a Dragon Bridge boy up in the rebel camp. Hulda's eldest. She'd give her right arm for a word from him, and I hear he's written one he hasn't the nerve to send.
story.skycraft.q.pl_haknirs_shoal.desc: The articles of Haknir Death-Brand's crew bind his drowned oarsmen to their benches through a brand-iron kept in the captain's chest. As long as it lies there, they row.
story.skycraft.q.pl_haknirs_shoal.o0.tex: Lay the drowned oarsmen of the Death-Brand to rest
story.skycraft.q.pl_haknirs_shoal.o2.jou: With the brand-iron out of the chest, the water around the wreck is finally still.
story.skycraft.q.pl_haknirs_shoal.o2.tex: Take the brand-iron from the captain's chest
story.skycraft.q.pl_haknirs_shoal.outro: The fishermen of the north shore say the shoal is quiet now. One of them swears he heard thirty-one voices sigh at once, the night the iron left the wreck.
story.skycraft.q.pl_haknirs_shoal.pitch: On still nights you can hear oars at Haknir's Shoal. The old crew swore an oath on some iron of the captain's. Take the iron out of the wreck, they say, and the oars will stop.
story.skycraft.q.pl_haknirs_shoal.title: Leave the Oar
story.skycraft.q.pl_halldirs_cairn.desc: Bersi's son Thorvi lost his dead mother's pendant to the warden of Halldir's Cairn. Bersi believes the boy's nightmares will end only when it is returned.
story.skycraft.q.pl_halldirs_cairn.o1.te: Defeat the warden in the iron mask
story.skycraft.q.pl_halldirs_cairn.o2.jo: The warden wore a dozen trinkets taken from trespassers over the centuries. The little bronze hammer was the newest.
story.skycraft.q.pl_halldirs_cairn.o2.te: Take Signy's pendant from the warden
story.skycraft.q.pl_halldirs_cairn.o3.re: That's hers. That's... Thorvi! Come here, son. No, it's all right, it's warm now, see? I'll make a box for it. A good box, with a lock. And I'll make you a bow, since you're so set on that archer girl in the hills.
story.skycraft.q.pl_halldirs_cairn.o3.te: Return the pendant to Bersi in Falkreath
story.skycraft.q.pl_halldirs_cairn.offer: You look like you haven't slept, carpenter.
story.skycraft.q.pl_halldirs_cairn.outro: Thorvi sleeps through the night for the first time in a month, and wakes asking when he can start archery lessons.
story.skycraft.q.pl_halldirs_cairn.pitch: My boy Thorvi went into Halldir's Cairn on a dare. He came out, thank Arkay, but he left his mother's pendant behind. He says a dead man in an iron mask took it from his neck. He hasn't slept a night since. Please. Bring it back, and maybe the dreams will stop.
story.skycraft.q.pl_halldirs_cairn.title: Signy's Pendant
story.skycraft.q.pl_halted_stream_camp.d: Bandits at Halted Stream Camp are working an old mine with farmhands taken from Loreius Farm. Their chief, Brattvar Stone-Hand, keeps the key to the chains on his belt.
story.skycraft.q.pl_halted_stream_camp.o: Clear the bandits from Halted Stream Camp
Ulf and Asbjorn of Loreius Farm are free. They ran for home without stopping to thank me, which I can hardly blame them for.
Take the shackle key and free the miners
The miners of Loreius Farm made it home. The mine at Halted Stream has fallen silent.
story.skycraft.q.pl_halted_stream_camp.p: Vantus Loreius thinks his missing farmhands ran off. They didn't. The bandits at Halted Stream have them digging in chains. Someone ought to go and break those chains.
story.skycraft.q.pl_hamvirs_rest.desc: A grave-robber's notes tell of his friend Skeggi, left behind in Hamvir's Rest when the dead chieftain woke. He begs anyone brave enough to put Hamvir down.
story.skycraft.q.pl_hamvirs_rest.o1.text: Put Hamvir the Patient back to rest
story.skycraft.q.pl_hamvirs_rest.o2.jour: Skeggi lay at the foot of Hamvir's throne. I left the axe across the chieftain's knees, where it belongs, and took only the boy's luck-charm.
story.skycraft.q.pl_hamvirs_rest.outro: Hamvir waits again, his axe across his knees. Skeggi's charm should go to someone who will bury it.
story.skycraft.q.pl_hamvirs_rest.pitch: Two robbers went into Hamvir's Rest after an old axe. One came out screaming. If you've got a strong arm, the dead in there need putting back to bed.
story.skycraft.q.pl_hamvirs_rest.title: Hamvir Does Not Rest
story.skycraft.q.pl_harmugstahl.desc: A shepherd's note found in Harmugstahl names the mage Ostrel Vane, who feeds travellers to the giant spiders he breeds behind the fort's walls.
story.skycraft.q.pl_harmugstahl.o3.journ: Vane's notes describe glyphs that bind beasts to a place. The College would want them. Perhaps nobody should have them.
story.skycraft.q.pl_harmugstahl.outro: Without its master, Harmugstahl is quiet. The webs in the walls will take years to fall.
story.skycraft.q.pl_harmugstahl.pitch: Shepherd from Karthwasten took sheep to the wizard at Harmugstahl and never came back. His wife won't hear he ran off. Something's eating people in that fort, and it isn't the wizard. Not directly.
story.skycraft.q.pl_harmugstahl.title: The Spider-Wright
story.skycraft.q.pl_helas_folly.desc: Captain Hela of the frozen ship Hela's Folly hid a strongbox of silver plate ashore before her crew died in the ice. Her last note describes where.
story.skycraft.q.pl_helas_folly.o0.text: Board the wreck of Hela's Folly
story.skycraft.q.pl_helas_folly.o1.journ: Wrapped in an old mainsail, weighted with the ship's bell: Hela's silver plate. Most of it is tarnished past saving, but a fine silver ring was packed among it.
story.skycraft.q.pl_helas_folly.o1.text: Dig up the plate by the crooked doorway of rock
story.skycraft.q.pl_helas_folly.outro: You drink to Hela Wave-Bride, who was right about the route and wrong about the weather.
story.skycraft.q.pl_helas_folly.pitch: They say the captain of Hela's Folly buried her cargo somewhere on the shore before the ice took her. Nobody's ever found it. Nobody's tried very hard, either.
story.skycraft.q.pl_helas_folly.title: Hela's Plate
story.skycraft.q.pl_helgen.desc: Ylva, a refugee from Helgen living in Riverwood, asks you to recover her father's strongbox from beneath his forge before looters take it.
story.skycraft.q.pl_helgen.o0.text: Go to the ruins of Helgen
story.skycraft.q.pl_helgen.o1.journal: The scavengers were already prying at the forge stones. The box is heavy and still warm from the ash.
story.skycraft.q.pl_helgen.o1.text: Find Torolf's strongbox under the smithy by the north gate
story.skycraft.q.pl_helgen.o2.reply: It's his mark on the lid. He made the lock himself. Here's Mother's ring... and the wedding money. He saved it for years, and I'm not even promised to anyone. Take a share. He'd want you paid. He always paid his debts.
story.skycraft.q.pl_helgen.o2.text: Bring the strongbox to Ylva in Riverwood
story.skycraft.q.pl_helgen.outro: Ylva wears her mother's ring on a cord around her neck, and she has stopped asking travellers about Helgen.
story.skycraft.q.pl_helgen.pitch: My father was the smith by the north gate. He kept a strongbox under the forge floor with my mother's ring in it. I can't go back there. I've tried; I get as far as the bridge and my legs stop. Scavengers are picking the town clean. Please, before they find it.
story.skycraft.q.pl_helgen.title: What the Fire Left
story.skycraft.q.pl_high_gate_ruins.desc: Surveyor Decimus Calvo of the Imperial Geographic Society went deeper into High Gate Ruins to finish his map. His satchel holds the only copy.
story.skycraft.q.pl_high_gate_ruins.o0.j: Calvo died at his drawing board in the last chamber, pencil still in hand. The map is finished except for one room.
story.skycraft.q.pl_high_gate_ruins.o1.t: Defeat the gate-warden of the old cult
story.skycraft.q.pl_high_gate_ruins.o2.t: Bring the map to the Legion at the Pale Imperial Camp
story.skycraft.q.pl_high_gate_ruins.outr: The Society will publish Calvo's map with a black border. The last room is marked simply: 'Do not.'
story.skycraft.q.pl_high_gate_ruins.pitc: There was an Imperial mapmaker went into High Gate Ruins. Wouldn't leave without finishing his map. I suppose he's finished now, one way or the other.
story.skycraft.q.pl_highpoint_tower.desc: The Telvanni wizard Arvyn Hlervu left a guardian of fire and ash in Highpoint Tower with one order: let no one up the stair who is not him. He never came back, and it never stopped walking.
story.skycraft.q.pl_highpoint_tower.o0.t: Unbind the guardian in the top chamber
story.skycraft.q.pl_highpoint_tower.o1.j: The grimoire is full of star charts and pages of notes on the fires of Red Mountain. Arvyn was right: the mountain is only sleeping.
story.skycraft.q.pl_highpoint_tower.o1.t: Take Arvyn's grimoire from the top chamber
story.skycraft.q.pl_highpoint_tower.outr: The stair of Highpoint Tower is quiet. Whatever Arvyn found out about Red Mountain, you are now the only one who knows it.
story.skycraft.q.pl_highpoint_tower.pitc: Something burning walks round and round the top of Highpoint Tower. The wizard who left it there has been gone eleven years. His books are still up there, if you can get past his watchdog.
story.skycraft.q.pl_hillgrunds_tomb.desc: A grave-robber stole Hillgrund's drinking horn from his bier and woke the tomb. Hillgrund's descendants can no longer bury their dead there.
story.skycraft.q.pl_hillgrunds_tomb.o0.j: The robber never left the side passage. The horn lay in his lap.
story.skycraft.q.pl_hillgrunds_tomb.o0.t: Find the stolen horn in the side passage
story.skycraft.q.pl_hillgrunds_tomb.o2.j: The horn is back on the bier. The tomb is silent.
story.skycraft.q.pl_hillgrunds_tomb.o2.t: Return the horn to Hillgrund's bier
story.skycraft.q.pl_hillgrunds_tomb.outr: In spring, Ingrun Hillgrund-Kin lays Torvar's urn with the rest of the line. Nothing stirs.
story.skycraft.q.pl_hillgrunds_tomb.pitc: Hillgrund's kin can't lay their dead in the old tomb anymore. Something's awake in there, and they say it's looking for a stolen horn.
story.skycraft.q.pl_hobs_fall_cave.desc: Vinicia Sallus, expelled from the College for necromancy, stole a restricted book from the Arcanaeum and now raises the drowned in Hob's Fall Cave.
story.skycraft.q.pl_hobs_fall_cave.o2.te: Recover the Concordance of the Unquiet
story.skycraft.q.pl_hobs_fall_cave.o3.re: Oh, the Arcanaeum's keeper will be thrilled. Thrilled is perhaps strong. He will grunt slightly less. I always said she had talent. I also always said she would end badly. I dislike being right about both.
story.skycraft.q.pl_hobs_fall_cave.o3.te: Return the book to the College through Quaestor Vesk
story.skycraft.q.pl_hobs_fall_cave.o3.to: The Concordance of the Unquiet, from Hob's Fall.
story.skycraft.q.pl_hobs_fall_cave.outro: The Legion camp's lost patrols are buried properly this time, on land.
story.skycraft.q.pl_hobs_fall_cave.pitch: There's a woman in Hob's Fall raising the drowned. The College threw her out years back. Now the Legion patrols keep disappearing and turning up on the beach, standing in the surf.
story.skycraft.q.pl_hobs_fall_cave.title: The Concordance of the Unquiet
story.skycraft.q.pl_honeystrand_cave.des: A forgetful beekeeper hid his wax money near Honeystrand Cave, thirty paces east under a flat stone, where the bears are less likely to dig.
Under the flat stone: a pouch of wax money and a gold ring. A bear watched me dig, just as the note promised.
Dig under the flat stone thirty paces east of Honeystrand Cave
story.skycraft.q.pl_honeystrand_cave.out: Rolf's stash is found. He'll be digging in the wrong place for a while yet.
story.skycraft.q.pl_honeystrand_cave.pit: Rolf the beekeeper buried his coin by Honeystrand Cave and forgot where. He's been digging up half the hillside. Bears watch him do it.
story.skycraft.q.pl_horker_island.desc: A salvager buried the purser's coin from Haknir Death-Brand's ship on Horker Island, under the flat stone where the old bull horker sleeps, twenty paces north of the island's middle.
story.skycraft.q.pl_horker_island.o1.jou: Under the stone: a tarred purse of coin and a gold ring, and the old bull horker very offended about it.
story.skycraft.q.pl_horker_island.o1.tex: Dig under the old bull's sleeping stone
story.skycraft.q.pl_horker_island.outro: Sigrid never came back in the spring. The old bull, the Skaal say, has found a new stone to sleep on, and he is sulking.
story.skycraft.q.pl_horker_island.pitch: Sigrid Net-Mender buried something on Horker Island before she drowned. Everyone knows it. Nobody wants to argue with the old bull horker about it.
story.skycraft.q.pl_horker_island.title: Under the Old Bull
story.skycraft.q.pl_hrothmunds_barrow.de: Masked cultists are digging in Hrothmund's Barrow for a key buried with the turncoat Hrothmund, a key to a door their Master once used. Their leader, Brother Ulfgar, must not find it first.
story.skycraft.q.pl_hrothmunds_barrow.o0: Fight through the cultists and the barrow's dead
story.skycraft.q.pl_hrothmunds_barrow.o2: Take Hrothmund's key before anyone else can
story.skycraft.q.pl_hrothmunds_barrow.o3: It is warm. Iron should not be warm. We will take it far out on the ice where the sea is deepest and give it back to the All-Maker. Whoever wanted it can go and ask him.
Give the key to the Skaal for safe keeping
The masked ones were digging for this.
story.skycraft.q.pl_hrothmunds_barrow.ou: The key is somewhere under the Sea of Ghosts. The cultists will find other doors; this one, at least, is shut.
story.skycraft.q.pl_hrothmunds_barrow.pi: Masked folk with lanterns are going in and out of Hrothmund's Barrow, digging for something. The same masks as those that attacked travellers at the docks. Whatever they want, they shouldn't have it.
story.skycraft.q.pl_ironback_hideout.des: The Talos faithful of the Ironback Hideout hid an iron icon of Talos under their hearthstone before the Thalmor came. The embassy still watches the cabin.
The icon was where Sigrid said, heavy and cold and rough. The watchers will not report it now.
Lift the hearthstone and take the icon to safety
story.skycraft.q.pl_ironback_hideout.out: The icon is in your keeping now. Somewhere in Haafingar, an old man's prayer has been answered.
story.skycraft.q.pl_ironback_hideout.pit: The faithful at Ironback hid something under their hearth before the elves came. It's still there, they say, and so are the elves some nights. If you remember the Ninth, you know what to do.
story.skycraft.q.pl_ironbind_barrow.desc: Three brothers called the Lucky went into Ironbind Barrow. Only Thorkel came out. His brothers' pieces of their mother's luck-stone are still inside.
story.skycraft.q.pl_ironbind_barrow.o0.j: Bjorn died in the burial hall with both pieces in his fist.
story.skycraft.q.pl_ironbind_barrow.o0.t: Find Bjorn and the two pieces of the luck-stone
story.skycraft.q.pl_ironbind_barrow.o1.t: Lay the iron-masked warlord to rest
story.skycraft.q.pl_ironbind_barrow.o2.r: Whole again. Mother said it would bring us home. It brought me home, I suppose. Bjorn always said I'd be the last one standing at the bar. Let me buy you that drink.
story.skycraft.q.pl_ironbind_barrow.o2.t: Bring the pieces to Thorkel at Nightgate Inn
Bjorn kept Ivar's piece and his own. Here.
story.skycraft.q.pl_ironbind_barrow.outr: Thorkel goes home to his mother's farm. He does not call himself Lucky anymore.
story.skycraft.q.pl_ironbind_barrow.pitc: Thorkel the Lucky sits at Nightgate Inn every night drinking to his brothers. They're still inside Ironbind Barrow. He says he can't go home until the luck-stone's whole.
story.skycraft.q.pl_journeymans_nook.des: Brynja Stormquill, a cartographer mapping the north for the College, buried an emergency purse behind Journeyman's Nook.
Under the flat rock: Brynja's purse, a gold ring and a note. 'If you're reading this and I'm alive, run.'
Dig under the flat rock north of the Nook
story.skycraft.q.pl_journeymans_nook.out: Somewhere in the north, Brynja Stormquill is probably very annoyed.
story.skycraft.q.pl_journeymans_nook.pit: That mapmaker woman, Stormquill, she used to stop at Journeyman's Nook. Swore she'd hidden a purse out there for hard times. Haven't seen her in a while.
story.skycraft.q.pl_kagrenzel.desc: Legionary Gaius Septimus was lowered into the Kagrenzel shaft and never hauled up. His cohort token is still somewhere at the bottom.
story.skycraft.q.pl_kagrenzel.o1.journal: Gaius Septimus lay at the bottom of the shaft beside a sphere guardian that had been waiting four thousand years for something to cut. The token was still around his neck.
story.skycraft.q.pl_kagrenzel.outro: Sergeant Avitus will hang the token over the Eastmarch Imperial Camp's gate, beside the cut rope.
story.skycraft.q.pl_kagrenzel.pitch: The Imperials lowered a lad into the Kagrenzel shaft on a rope and pulled up only the rope. Their sergeant wants his cohort token back. Me, I'd just want him back.
story.skycraft.q.pl_kagrenzel.title: Two Hundred Feet of Rope
story.skycraft.q.pl_kagrumez.desc: Ulvo Nerano of Tel Mithryn wants the brass tuning key from the deepest resonance chamber of Kagrumez, a Dwemer ruin whose gem plinths wake its guardians when touched wrongly.
story.skycraft.q.pl_kagrumez.o0.text: Enter the resonance chambers of Kagrumez
story.skycraft.q.pl_kagrumez.o1.text: Silence the guardians the chambers wake
story.skycraft.q.pl_kagrumez.o2.text: Take the tuning key from the master plinth
story.skycraft.q.pl_kagrumez.o3.reply: It does, doesn't it? Listen. That is the note the Dwemer thought held the world together. A little flat, if you ask me. Here, your payment, and my undying gratitude, which as a Dunmer of modest means is worth slightly less than the payment.
story.skycraft.q.pl_kagrumez.o3.text: Bring the tuning key to Ulvo Nerano
story.skycraft.q.pl_kagrumez.offer: You said you needed someone sturdy?
story.skycraft.q.pl_kagrumez.outro: Ulvo has opened the inner doors of Kagrumez without a single sphere chasing him. He has written to Neloth about it. Neloth has written back one word, and Ulvo will not say what it was.
story.skycraft.q.pl_kagrumez.pitch: Precisely! In Kagrumez there is a brass tuning key on the master plinth of the deepest chamber. With it I can read the resonance chambers without guessing, and without being chased by spheres. I have guessed twice. Bring it to me and you will have advanced Dwemer scholarship more than Neloth has in a century.
story.skycraft.q.pl_kagrumez.title: The Tuning Key
story.skycraft.q.pl_kjenstag_ruins.desc: The runes at Kjenstag Ruins say the lantern-bearer's ghost walks because grave robbers stole his bronze horn. A Morthal guard saw the horn lying in the robbers' old camp nearby.
story.skycraft.q.pl_kjenstag_ruins.o0.jo: The horn hums in my hand like a held breath. The marsh-lights did not want me to have it.
story.skycraft.q.pl_kjenstag_ruins.o0.te: Find the bronze horn in the grave robbers' old camp
story.skycraft.q.pl_kjenstag_ruins.o1.jo: I set the horn on the fallen lintel. The lantern came across the circle, stopped, and went out. Far off, very faintly, something blew a single long note.
story.skycraft.q.pl_kjenstag_ruins.o1.te: Return the horn to the lantern-bearer at the stone circle
story.skycraft.q.pl_kjenstag_ruins.outro: No light walks Kjenstag now. The Morthal folk say the marsh is darker for it, and safer, and a little lonelier.
story.skycraft.q.pl_kjenstag_ruins.pitch: That light at Kjenstag? It's a dead man looking for his horn, the old stones say. Robbers took it. Guardsman Aslak says it's lying in the reeds right there. Somebody should just give the poor thing back.
story.skycraft.q.pl_kjenstag_ruins.title: The Lantern-Bearer's Horn
story.skycraft.q.pl_knifepoint_ridge.des: Jarl Siddgeir has posted a bounty on the bandit leader Hjolfrid Ashpine of Knifepoint Ridge. Bailiff Eirik in Falkreath will pay on proof of her death.
Hjolfrid fought to the last. Her scorched-handled knife will serve as proof.
That's her knife, right enough. Bolli's widow will sleep tonight. The Jarl will claim the credit, naturally. Here's your purse, and here's my thanks, which is worth less but is at least sincere.
Bring proof to Bailiff Eirik in Falkreath
Hjolfrid Ashpine is dead. Here's her knife.
story.skycraft.q.pl_knifepoint_ridge.out: The Half-Moon road is quieter. Somewhere in Bruma, a man waits for a letter that will never come.
story.skycraft.q.pl_knifepoint_ridge.pit: The Jarl's put a price on Hjolfrid Ashpine, at last. She runs Knifepoint Ridge and she killed the carter Bolli and his son. Bailiff Eirik pays on proof.
story.skycraft.q.pl_kolbjorn_barrow.desc: Neral Sadas, a farmer's son from Old Attius Farm, was trapped in Kolbjorn Barrow when a gallery collapsed. His diary says he is hiding behind the third pillar of a side chamber, and the dead are waking.
story.skycraft.q.pl_kolbjorn_barrow.o0.t: Find the collapsed gallery in Kolbjorn Barrow
story.skycraft.q.pl_kolbjorn_barrow.o1.t: Put down the barrow's waking warden
story.skycraft.q.pl_kolbjorn_barrow.o2.j: Neral is alive, half-starved and shaking. He gave me his digging pass to show his father, and he'll follow the cleared path out on his own.
story.skycraft.q.pl_kolbjorn_barrow.o2.t: Find Neral behind the third pillar
story.skycraft.q.pl_kolbjorn_barrow.o3.r: Alive? Alive! Then I'll kill the boy myself for frightening me. After supper. After a very large supper. Thank you, friend, from the bottom of my ash-caked heart.
story.skycraft.q.pl_kolbjorn_barrow.o3.t: Bring Neral's pass to Tilvur at Old Attius Farm
Neral's alive. He's walking home behind me.
story.skycraft.q.pl_kolbjorn_barrow.outr: Neral is home. Tilvur swears he'll never set foot in a barrow again. Neral is already asking whether Ralis Sedarys still owes him wages.
story.skycraft.q.pl_kolbjorn_barrow.pitc: Tilvur Sadas's boy is stuck down in Kolbjorn Barrow, behind a fallen gallery. The excavator says he's fine. The excavator says that about everything. Somebody ought to go and look.
story.skycraft.q.pl_kvatch.desc: Lucia Atrius of Anvil wrote to the masons of Kvatch: her family's seal-stone, carved with a swallow, was buried under a cellar flag in the glassblowers' lane the night the Gate opened.
story.skycraft.q.pl_kvatch.o0.text: Find the old glassblowers' lane beneath the cathedral
story.skycraft.q.pl_kvatch.o1.journal: Under the third flag, in a nest of skeevers, a grey stone with a swallow on it. It is warm, as though someone had held it a moment ago.
story.skycraft.q.pl_kvatch.o1.text: Dig under the third flag from the hearth for the Atrius seal-stone
story.skycraft.q.pl_kvatch.outro: You leave the swallow-stone at the masons' table with a note for Lucia Atrius of Anvil. Savlian Matius promises it will reach her. One thing, at least, did not melt.
story.skycraft.q.pl_kvatch.pitch: There's a letter pinned up at the masons' table from a woman in Anvil. Her family's seal-stone is buried somewhere in the old glassblowers' lane. The masons haven't time. Maybe you have.
story.skycraft.q.pl_kvatch.title: The Swallow-Stone
story.skycraft.q.pl_labyrinthian.desc: A College student named Teneras mapped the lines in Labyrinthian's floors that the dead will not cross, and hid his notebook under a loose slab in the hall of the broken masks.
story.skycraft.q.pl_labyrinthian.o1.jour: The notebook was under the slab, exactly as he said. The last pattern is unfinished: a word in the old tongue, half-drawn.
story.skycraft.q.pl_labyrinthian.o1.text: Find Teneras's notebook in the hall of the broken masks
story.skycraft.q.pl_labyrinthian.outro: Teneras's lines hold true. The College will want the notebook, and his tutor will have to admit he was wrong.
story.skycraft.q.pl_labyrinthian.pitch: Another College student lost in Labyrinthian, they say. This one left notes about lines in the floor that the dead won't cross. If those notes are real, they're worth more than gold to the next poor fool who goes in.
story.skycraft.q.pl_labyrinthian.title: The Pattern in the Floor
story.skycraft.q.pl_lakeview.desc: Gunnar Lake-Holm buried his family's savings under two leaning pines downhill of the Lakeview plot, toward the water, before he fled.
story.skycraft.q.pl_lakeview.o0.journal: The pot was where Gunnar said: two pines leaning together, the earth soft beneath them. Grandmother's gold ring lies on top of the coins.
story.skycraft.q.pl_lakeview.o0.text: Dig under the two leaning pines downhill of Lakeview
story.skycraft.q.pl_lakeview.outro: Gunnar never came back for it. Perhaps he knew he wouldn't.
story.skycraft.q.pl_lakeview.pitch: The Lake-Holms left that hill plot in a hurry. Gunnar always said he didn't trust Gray Pine Goods with his savings. If he didn't keep it in the house, he kept it in the ground.
story.skycraft.q.pl_lakeview.title: Where Money Sleeps
story.skycraft.q.pl_last_vigil.desc: The bandits at Last Vigil robbed a Black-Briar mead wagon and found something under the cask's false bottom that was never meant to be mead.
story.skycraft.q.pl_last_vigil.o0.journa: The cask is heavy and it clinks. Under the false bottom: bottles of Redwater skooma.
story.skycraft.q.pl_last_vigil.o0.text: Take the 'reserve' cask from Last Vigil
story.skycraft.q.pl_last_vigil.o1.reply: Red skooma. In a Briar cask. Mara's mercy. Maven will say it was planted, and half the court will believe her because she pays them to. But I'll write it down. Somebody has to start writing it down.
story.skycraft.q.pl_last_vigil.o1.text: Bring the cask to Ingrith in Riften
story.skycraft.q.pl_last_vigil.o1.topic: This came off a Black-Briar wagon. Look under the bottom.
story.skycraft.q.pl_last_vigil.outro: Ingrith has the cask and a page in her own ledger that starts with Redwater and ends with a black thorn.
story.skycraft.q.pl_last_vigil.pitch: Last Vigil hit a Black-Briar wagon, the mad fools. They say the cask they took isn't mead at all. Somebody ought to get it before Maven's men do.
story.skycraft.q.pl_last_vigil.title: The Reserve Cask
story.skycraft.q.pl_left_hand_mine.desc: Aurelia Salvius asked me to find her brother Lucan, lost in the closed deep drift of Left Hand Mine.
story.skycraft.q.pl_left_hand_mine.o0.te: Enter the deep drift of Left Hand Mine
story.skycraft.q.pl_left_hand_mine.o2.jo: Lucan Salvius was alive, thin and grinning, sitting very still behind the steam pipe with the pick across his knees. His hands shook too much to carry it, so he gave it to me.
story.skycraft.q.pl_left_hand_mine.o2.te: Find Lucan beyond the Dwarven door
story.skycraft.q.pl_left_hand_mine.o3.re: Alive? Alive! And he made you carry the pick, didn't he. Of course he did. Divines bless you. I'm baking the spiced bread tonight, all of it, and he is not getting any until he says thank you.
story.skycraft.q.pl_left_hand_mine.o3.te: Bring the pick to Aurelia at Salvius Farm
story.skycraft.q.pl_left_hand_mine.o3.to: Lucan's alive. He's on his way home.
story.skycraft.q.pl_left_hand_mine.outro: The Salvius pick hangs over the farmhouse door. Lucan says he will never go below the second timber frame again. Nobody believes him.
story.skycraft.q.pl_left_hand_mine.pitch: Lucan went back down the deep drift at Left Hand Mine for our father's pick after Skaggi closed it. The spiders came up through the old Dwarven cut. Skaggi won't send anyone. Would you?
story.skycraft.q.pl_left_hand_mine.title: Father's Pick
story.skycraft.q.pl_liars_retreat.desc: Hrefna, the mine clerk at Soljund's Sinkhole, wants her stolen moonstone back from the bandits at Liar's Retreat.
story.skycraft.q.pl_liars_retreat.o2.jou: The strongbox was exactly where Ottar's orders said it would be. The one honest thing he ever wrote.
story.skycraft.q.pl_liars_retreat.o3.rep: Thirty pieces, I'll count them twice. Pa will say I should have hired you in the first place. Pa will be right. Don't tell him I said so.
story.skycraft.q.pl_liars_retreat.o3.tex: Bring the moonstone to Hrefna at Soljund's Sinkhole
story.skycraft.q.pl_liars_retreat.offer: You said you were short of moonstone?
story.skycraft.q.pl_liars_retreat.outro: Soljund's Sinkhole sent its next shipment with an escort paid on arrival, not in advance.
story.skycraft.q.pl_liars_retreat.pitch: Short by thirty pieces and two escorts. Bandits at Liar's Retreat took the cart, and their chief, a talker called Sweet-Tongue Ottar, will swear on his mother's grave it went into the river. Bring back the strongbox and I'll pay you what the escorts were supposed to earn.
story.skycraft.q.pl_liars_retreat.title: Sweet-Tongue's Last Lie
story.skycraft.q.pl_lilmoth.desc: The last Imperial customs-master of Lilmoth sank his strongbox of thirty years' bribes off the old customs pier when the Empire left. His letter says where. The slaughterfish have kept it ever since.
story.skycraft.q.pl_lilmoth.o0.text: Find the end of the old customs pier in Lilmoth harbour
story.skycraft.q.pl_lilmoth.o1.journal: The strongbox comes up black with mud and heavier than any honest box should be. Two centuries of bribes, and every coin stamped with a dead Emperor's face.
story.skycraft.q.pl_lilmoth.o1.text: Raise the customs-master's strongbox from the mud
story.skycraft.q.pl_lilmoth.outro: The Saxhleel dock-workers watch you open the box and laugh until they have to sit down. 'Imperial gold,' one says, 'paid to an Imperial, to cheat the marsh. And now the marsh gives it to you.' He seems to think that is the best joke in Lilmoth.
story.skycraft.q.pl_lilmoth.pitch: Every diver in Lilmoth's gone after that old Imperial strongbox. It's off the end of the customs pier, in the shadow of the harbour tower. The fish there are the size of dogs. Bring a long hook and a short temper.
story.skycraft.q.pl_lilmoth.title: The Customs-Master's Strongbox
story.skycraft.q.pl_lost_echo_cave.desc: Edda Fairvoice, a student bard, left her lute wedged in the rocks of Lost Echo Cave while hiding from blind hunters that track by sound.
story.skycraft.q.pl_lost_echo_cave.o1.jo: The lute was where Edda left it. Her last candle was beside it, burned down to nothing.
story.skycraft.q.pl_lost_echo_cave.outro: The cave is quieter now. Somewhere in Solitude, the Bards College will want Edda's lute back on its wall.
story.skycraft.q.pl_lost_echo_cave.pitch: A student from the Bards College went into Lost Echo Cave to compose. Her lute's still down there, they say. The College would pay to have it home, and so would her mother.
story.skycraft.q.pl_lost_echo_cave.title: The Song That Came Back
Teodric, a minstrel of the Bards College, is held in a cage above the falls at Lost Valley Redoubt, singing nightly for the hagraven Kerath Burnt-Feather. She is running out of patience.
Cut through the Forsworn guarding the falls
Teodric climbed out of his cage, bowed with great ceremony, and set off for Solitude singing a brand-new song about a hero at Bard's Leap.
Kill Kerath Burnt-Feather and take her keys
The Bards College has a new ballad this season. It is mostly accurate.
The crones at Lost Valley Redoubt grabbed a minstrel from the Bards College. They keep him singing for his supper. Word is the old hag burned his lute. He hasn't got many songs left.
story.skycraft.q.pl_lower_steepfall_burr: The trapper Asgeir Coldhand tracked a white-backed troll called Greyback to the Lower Steepfall Burrow and never came back. His father's hunting horn went with him.
Asgeir's bones lay at the back of the den, his horn still in his hand. He never blew it.
Greyback's white hide fetches a fine price in Solitude. Asgeir's horn hangs over the bar at the Winking Skeever, where he always meant it to be.
Asgeir Coldhand went after the white troll at Steepfall. Swore he'd hang its hide in the Winking Skeever. Somebody ought to finish the hunt, and bring his horn home.
story.skycraft.q.pl_lunds_hut.desc: Lund the trapper went to deal with a bold wolf pack near his hut north-west of Rorikstead and never returned. His wife Hjalla needs to know what happened.
story.skycraft.q.pl_lunds_hut.o0.journal: The hut was empty, the fire long cold. Lund's journal speaks of a wolf den in the rocks above, and a grey leader with a white blaze.
story.skycraft.q.pl_lunds_hut.o1.journal: At the den lay what was left of Lund, his bow still strung. I took his ring for Hjalla.
story.skycraft.q.pl_lunds_hut.o1.text: Hunt down the white-blazed pack leader
story.skycraft.q.pl_lunds_hut.o2.reply: I knew. I knew when the snow came and he didn't. But knowing and being told are different things. Thank you for bringing him back to me, this much of him.
story.skycraft.q.pl_lunds_hut.o2.text: Bring Lund's ring to Hjalla in Rorikstead
story.skycraft.q.pl_lunds_hut.outro: Hjalla wears Lund's ring on a cord now. She has sold his traps, but not his bow.
story.skycraft.q.pl_lunds_hut.pitch: My husband, Lund. He went up to his hut in the hills to deal with a wolf pack and he hasn't come down. It's been two weeks. Nobody here will go. Please. Even if it's bad news, I need to know.
story.skycraft.q.pl_lunds_hut.title: The Trapper's Wife
story.skycraft.q.pl_maras_eye_pond.desc: Kjeld the trapper buried thirty years of savings under a flat mossy stone on the west bank of Mara's Eye Pond, meaning them for his sister.
story.skycraft.q.pl_maras_eye_pond.o0.te: Find the hand-shaped moss on the west bank of Mara's Eye Pond
story.skycraft.q.pl_maras_eye_pond.o1.jo: Under the stone: an iron box, a purse of old septims, and his mother's gold ring wrapped in a scrap of fox fur. Kjeld's sister, Rannveig, would want the ring at least.
story.skycraft.q.pl_maras_eye_pond.outro: The trapper's thirty years fit in one hand. It seems too little, and somehow enough.
story.skycraft.q.pl_maras_eye_pond.pitch: Kjeld the trapper left the Riverside Shack in a hurry and never reached Kynesgrove. He used to say his savings were safer by the water than in any town. Maybe somebody should check the pond.
story.skycraft.q.pl_maras_eye_pond.title: A Trapper's Thirty Years
story.skycraft.q.pl_mistwatch.desc: Bandits at Mistwatch rob only the gold carts from the Goldenrock Mine. Someone at Darkwater Crossing, who signs himself 'E.', is selling them the schedule.
story.skycraft.q.pl_mistwatch.o0.text: Fight your way up Mistwatch tower
story.skycraft.q.pl_mistwatch.o1.journal: Brolfr's tally sheet names payments to 'E.' at Darkwater Crossing. The last entry says E. stopped sending word in Frostfall, the same week Eirik the driver came home with an arrow in his shoulder.
story.skycraft.q.pl_mistwatch.o2.c0.labe: Name him. He sold you out and he should answer for it.
story.skycraft.q.pl_mistwatch.o2.c0.repl: Then he answers to the Jarl's steward, not to me. I'll not have the Crossing say I hanged my own man. Thank you. I think.
story.skycraft.q.pl_mistwatch.o2.c1.labe: Burn it. He stopped, and he bled for it.
story.skycraft.q.pl_mistwatch.o2.c1.repl: ...Aye. A man who takes an arrow for the thing he sold has paid something already. I'll burn it, and I'll watch him load the next cart. Closely.
story.skycraft.q.pl_mistwatch.o2.reply: Show me. ...E. Eirik. My own driver. He took an arrow for that cart. Did he take it because he stopped telling them? Tell me what you think I should do.
story.skycraft.q.pl_mistwatch.o2.text: Bring the tally sheet to Haldis Copperhand
story.skycraft.q.pl_mistwatch.o2.topic: I know who's been selling your carts.
story.skycraft.q.pl_mistwatch.outro: The gold carts from Darkwater Crossing pass Mistwatch unmolested, for now.
story.skycraft.q.pl_mistwatch.pitch: The Mistwatch bandits always know which Darkwater cart carries gold. Haldis Copperhand will pay well for the tally sheet they keep. She wants to know which neighbour is selling her.
story.skycraft.q.pl_mistwatch.title: The Friend at the Crossing
story.skycraft.q.pl_moldering_ruins.desc: A Rorikstead boy named Agnar came back from the Moldering Ruins struck silent, leaving his father's knife behind. His sister Svala believes that if the knife returns, some of Agnar will too.
story.skycraft.q.pl_moldering_ruins.o0.j: The knife lay at the foot of a stone throne. On the throne sat a draugr in a bronze crown, eyes open, watching. I did not close them.
story.skycraft.q.pl_moldering_ruins.o0.t: Find Agnar's knife in the Moldering Ruins
story.skycraft.q.pl_moldering_ruins.o1.r: You went in there? For a little knife? I'll give it to him tonight. Even if he doesn't speak, I know he'll hold it. Thank you, truly.
story.skycraft.q.pl_moldering_ruins.o1.t: Bring the knife to Svala in Rorikstead
story.skycraft.q.pl_moldering_ruins.outr: Svala says Agnar spoke one word the night he got his knife back: 'Watching.' Then he slept through till morning for the first time in weeks.
story.skycraft.q.pl_moldering_ruins.pitc: Svala's little brother went into the Moldering Ruins after a lamb and came out not speaking. He left his knife in there. She thinks getting it back might help him. Children are funny that way.
story.skycraft.q.pl_morvunskar.desc: Elsbet, a young mage from Winterhold, followed the expelled conjurer Ralis Varvel to Morvunskar. His notes say he means to 'tether' summoned things to her.
story.skycraft.q.pl_morvunskar.o0.text: Break through Varvel's followers at Morvunskar
story.skycraft.q.pl_morvunskar.o1.text: Stop Ralis Varvel before the tethering
story.skycraft.q.pl_morvunskar.o2.journa: Elsbet was chained in the cellar beside the north spring, alive and furious. She took the key from me without a word, and then, at the door, she said: 'Burn the notes. Or don't. But never read them aloud.'
story.skycraft.q.pl_morvunskar.outro: Elsbet walked north toward Winterhold, and the spring under Morvunskar has cooled a little.
story.skycraft.q.pl_morvunskar.pitch: There was a girl from Winterhold, Elsbet, went to study with the mages at Morvunskar. Her letters stopped in Hearthfire. Someone ought to look, before the snows close the College road.
story.skycraft.q.pl_morvunskar.title: The Living Anchor
story.skycraft.q.pl_moss_mother_cavern.d: Hroa and her brother Asvald vanished into Moss Mother Cavern. Asvald asked that whoever finds Hroa's ash bow lay it on the hearth at Hunter's Rest.
story.skycraft.q.pl_moss_mother_cavern.o: Brother and sister lie together under the roots at the back of the cavern. The bow was in Hroa's hands.
Lay Hroa's bow on the hearth at Hunter's Rest
The bow rests on the hearth. Someone will light the fire again; hunters always do.
story.skycraft.q.pl_moss_mother_cavern.p: Hroa of Hunter's Rest followed a wounded stag into Moss Mother Cavern. Her brother Asvald went in after her. Neither came out, and the hearth at the Rest has gone cold.
story.skycraft.q.pl_mount_anthor.desc: A grey dragon has made its roost on the word wall of Mount Anthor and is devouring the flocks of the high pastures. A shepherd's son means to fight it with an axe.
story.skycraft.q.pl_mount_anthor.o1.jour: The dragon of Mount Anthor is dead. Ragna's son will have to find something else to fight.
story.skycraft.q.pl_mount_anthor.o1.text: Slay the dragon of Mount Anthor
story.skycraft.q.pl_mount_anthor.outro: Ragna gives back her son's axe. He has decided to become a shepherd after all.
story.skycraft.q.pl_mount_anthor.pitch: There's a dragon sitting on the old wall up on Mount Anthor, eating every sheep in the valley. Ragna's boy wants to go up with an axe. Somebody had better get there first.
story.skycraft.q.pl_mount_anthor.title: The Shepherd's Dragon
story.skycraft.q.pl_movarths_lair.desc: Brynja of Morthal believes her husband Geirlund was taken by vampires into Movarth's Lair, north-east of town.
story.skycraft.q.pl_movarths_lair.o0.tex: Find Movarth's Lair in the marsh
story.skycraft.q.pl_movarths_lair.o2.jou: Geirlund was beyond saving. Vessa wore his ring on a string about her neck. His last pages asked for fire, and I gave the lair fire.
story.skycraft.q.pl_movarths_lair.o3.rep: I knew it. I knew it wasn't a bear. ...Thank you. I'll wear it on my own hand now, next to mine. Morthal can say what it likes about hoping.
story.skycraft.q.pl_movarths_lair.o3.tex: Bring the ring to Brynja in Morthal
story.skycraft.q.pl_movarths_lair.o3.top: Geirlund's ring. He was thinking of you, at the end.
story.skycraft.q.pl_movarths_lair.outro: Brynja keeps hunting the marsh, two rings on one hand and a silver knife at her belt. The townsfolk stop telling her what to hope.
story.skycraft.q.pl_movarths_lair.pitch: Geirlund went to check his traps and left his bow on the path to Movarth's Lair, strung and set down neat as you please. That's no bear. Something asked him to put it down. I've a silver knife and no courage left. You look like you have both.
story.skycraft.q.pl_movarths_lair.title: Brynja's Vow
story.skycraft.q.pl_mzinchaleft.desc: Sigrun Ice-Vein, foreman of the Rockwallow Mine at Stonehills, wants to know what became of her brother Knud and his crew in the Dwemer ruin of Mzinchaleft.
story.skycraft.q.pl_mzinchaleft.o1.journ: The token lay by the brass pillar with the broken arm. Knud's journal lay a little further on, in the lift-house. He did not reach the door.
story.skycraft.q.pl_mzinchaleft.o1.text: Find Knud's miner's token past the first great door
story.skycraft.q.pl_mzinchaleft.o2.reply: Even at the end he was giving orders. ...We'll brick it tonight. All of us. And I'll put this on the shift board, where his name always was.
story.skycraft.q.pl_mzinchaleft.o2.text: Bring the token to Sigrun at Stonehills
story.skycraft.q.pl_mzinchaleft.o2.topic: Knud's token. And his last words: brick up the east tunnel.
story.skycraft.q.pl_mzinchaleft.offer: Is something wrong at the mine?
story.skycraft.q.pl_mzinchaleft.outro: The east tunnel of the Rockwallow Mine is bricked and blessed. Sigrun Ice-Vein never goes below the third level again.
story.skycraft.q.pl_mzinchaleft.pitch: I sent five men into Mzinchaleft after Dwemer metal. My brother Knud led them. One came back, and he only talks to his bed board. He says Knud gave him a token for me and he dropped it running, past the first great door. I want it. I want to know. And I'm too much of a coward to go myself.
story.skycraft.q.pl_mzinchaleft.title: Ice-Vein's Brother
story.skycraft.q.pl_mzulft.desc: Livia Cassinia of the Imperial Geographical Society went into Mzulft in Hearthfire to study a Dwemer resonance plate. She has not come out. Her partner Bertrand Vanne waits at Kynesgrove.
story.skycraft.q.pl_mzulft.o0.text: Enter Mzulft and follow Livia's trail
story.skycraft.q.pl_mzulft.o1.text: Fight past the Falmer of the boiler halls
story.skycraft.q.pl_mzulft.o2.journal: Livia's body lay at the foot of the great plate. Her journal was still in her hand, her charcoal rubbing folded inside. The Falmer had built their shrine around her.
story.skycraft.q.pl_mzulft.o2.text: Find Livia's journal and her rubbing of the plate
story.skycraft.q.pl_mzulft.o3.reply: I know. I knew when I saw you come in the door with her book under your arm. ...She would want this published. I will see that it is, with her name first. It was always her name first.
story.skycraft.q.pl_mzulft.o3.text: Bring Livia's journal to Bertrand Vanne at Kynesgrove
story.skycraft.q.pl_mzulft.outro: The Imperial Geographical Society will one day print 'On the Tuning of the Earth', by L. Cassinia, with a foreword by B. Vanne.
story.skycraft.q.pl_mzulft.pitch: A Breton scholar is sitting in the Braidwood Inn every night waiting for his partner, a lady who went into Mzulft in Hearthfire. It's Frostfall. Somebody should go and look, for his sake.
story.skycraft.q.pl_mzulft.title: The Tuning of the Earth
story.skycraft.q.pl_necrom.desc: Grave-robbers have broken urns in Necrom's catacombs and sold the ashes to Daedra-worshippers. Mortician Mirvala Sadri wants the urn of the mortuary's founder, Llaren Indavel, brought home from the robbers' camp behind the Mad God's shrine.
story.skycraft.q.pl_necrom.o0.text: Find the grave-robbers' camp behind the Mad God's shrine
story.skycraft.q.pl_necrom.o1.text: Kill Vedam the Urn-Breaker and his gang
story.skycraft.q.pl_necrom.o2.journal: The urn is cracked but sealed. As you lift it, it grows heavier, then lighter, as if someone inside had decided you would do.
story.skycraft.q.pl_necrom.o2.text: Recover the urn of Ancestor Llaren Indavel
story.skycraft.q.pl_necrom.o3.reply: Oh, thank the Three. And thank you. Listen. Do you hear that? Nothing. For the first time in a month, the catacombs are quiet. He approves of you. That is not a small thing. He approves of almost no one.
story.skycraft.q.pl_necrom.o3.text: Return the urn to Mortician Mirvala in Necrom
story.skycraft.q.pl_necrom.outro: Your name is written, small, in the margin of the mortuary's book of benefactors. The priests say that in Necrom, the dead read the margins.
story.skycraft.q.pl_necrom.pitch: Somebody's stealing our dead. The mortician's frantic, and old Llaren's urn is gone, the founder himself. The robbers camp behind the Mad God's shrine on the pilgrim road. Mirvala at the mortuary will pay. Llaren won't, but he'll stop rattling the walls.
story.skycraft.q.pl_necrom.title: The Displeased Ancestor
story.skycraft.q.pl_nilheim.desc: The bandits of Nilheim robbed Oddvar the Pilgrim of a brass votive bell he meant to ring at High Hrothgar.
story.skycraft.q.pl_nilheim.o0.text: Deal with Svidi Half-Hand at Nilheim
story.skycraft.q.pl_nilheim.o2.reply: Ha! Listen to it. Just the same as when I was a boy. I'll ring it at the top for Father, and once more for you. The Greybeards will grumble. Let them.
story.skycraft.q.pl_nilheim.o2.text: Return the bell to Oddvar in Ivarstead
story.skycraft.q.pl_nilheim.o2.topic: Your bell. Svidi won't be robbing pilgrims again.
story.skycraft.q.pl_nilheim.outro: Oddvar has set off up the Seven Thousand Steps with his bell. If the wind is right, Ivarstead may hear it.
story.skycraft.q.pl_nilheim.pitch: Bandits at Nilheim took my father's bell. I meant to ring it at the top of the Steps, for his soul. I'm too old to fight, and too stubborn to go home without it.
story.skycraft.q.pl_nilheim.title: The Votive Bell
story.skycraft.q.pl_north_shriekwind_bas: The draugr chieftain Hjalti stirs in North Shriekwind Bastion and calls for his brother Eyvind. The barrow door stands open.
Hjalti's last shout was his brother's name. The wind over Falkreath is only wind again.
Guardsman Leif takes the north road patrol again, and admits the wind sounds almost friendly now.
The wind from North Shriekwind is calling a name, and the guard who heard it won't go back. Old Hjalti's woken up, Runil thinks, and means to fetch his brother from the south barrow.
story.skycraft.q.pl_northwatch_keep.desc: The Thalmor register at Northwatch Keep lists an old priest of Talos, Hjorvar the Grey, taken from the Ironback Hideout. His interrogator is Justiciar Ancarion.
story.skycraft.q.pl_northwatch_keep.o3.j: Hjorvar died in his cell two days ago, his prayer still scratched fresh into the wall. He never gave them a single name. His iron beads were in his hand.
story.skycraft.q.pl_northwatch_keep.o3.t: Find what became of Hjorvar the Grey
story.skycraft.q.pl_northwatch_keep.outr: Word reaches the Ironback faithful that Hjorvar died silent. On the first Sundas of the next month, they meet again.
story.skycraft.q.pl_northwatch_keep.pitc: There's an old Talos priest the elves took to Northwatch. Hjorvar. Everyone who prayed with him is still free, because he hasn't talked. Somebody ought to make sure the elf asking the questions stops asking.
story.skycraft.q.pl_northwind_mine.desc: Old Brandulf, once foreman of Northwind Mine, is dying, and asks every night for his father's silver-banded pick. He left it in the third gallery when the chaurus came.
story.skycraft.q.pl_northwind_mine.o0.te: Find the heirloom pick in the third gallery
story.skycraft.q.pl_northwind_mine.o1.re: That's it. That's the one. He'll weep, and then he'll shout at me for not fetching it myself. Thank you. He can go to Sovngarde with it now, like he wanted.
story.skycraft.q.pl_northwind_mine.o1.te: Bring the pick to Brandulf the Younger at Shor's Stone
story.skycraft.q.pl_northwind_mine.o1.to: Your great-grandfather's pick. Hearth, ore, home.
story.skycraft.q.pl_northwind_mine.outro: Old Brandulf has his father's pick across his knees. He says he'll be buried with it, and that I'm welcome at the funeral.
story.skycraft.q.pl_northwind_mine.pitch: Old Brandulf at Shor's Stone wants his father's pick from Northwind Mine before he dies. Chaurus in there, mind. His grandson tried. His grandson came back fast.
story.skycraft.q.pl_northwind_mine.title: Hearth, Ore, Home
story.skycraft.q.pl_orotheim.desc: The Orotheim gang charges a toll on the Rorikstead road and works those who can't pay in a pen inside their cave. Their chief keeps the pen key on his belt.
story.skycraft.q.pl_orotheim.o1.journal: Brodir's key opens the work-pen. Lars Eriksson and four others walk out into daylight, blinking.
story.skycraft.q.pl_orotheim.outro: The road to Rorikstead is free again. A few weeks later a cart of fresh bread arrives for you at the nearest inn, paid for by grateful farmers.
story.skycraft.q.pl_orotheim.pitch: The Orotheim gang's got farmhands from three villages working off a toll that never gets smaller. The chief keeps the key on his belt. It's not the sort of thing a key should be kept on.
story.skycraft.q.pl_orotheim.title: The Toll at Orotheim
story.skycraft.q.pl_orphan_rock.desc: A hagraven called Mother Thornclaw holds Orphan Rock and keeps the old cradle charm that once protected lost children. Ragna's brother paid her price and never came home.
story.skycraft.q.pl_orphan_rock.o2.journ: Ragna's brother lies at the foot of the rock, at peace. The cradle charm can go back where the foundling hung it.
story.skycraft.q.pl_orphan_rock.o2.text: Take back the birchwood cradle charm
story.skycraft.q.pl_orphan_rock.o3.text: Tell Ragna at North Skybound Watch, and give the charm to her fire
story.skycraft.q.pl_orphan_rock.outro: The beacon on North Skybound Watch burns one more night, and then Ragna lets it go out.
story.skycraft.q.pl_orphan_rock.pitch: Ragna lights a beacon on North Skybound Watch every night for her brother. He went to the hagraven on Orphan Rock for a cure. Someone ought to go up there and find out what it cost him.
story.skycraft.q.pl_orphan_rock.title: The Lost Are Ours
story.skycraft.q.pl_orphans_tear.desc: The last log of the Orphan's Tear says her captain chained the Company's pay chest to the bulkhead before she struck. It may still be aboard.
story.skycraft.q.pl_orphans_tear.o0.jour: The chest was where the captain said, chained to the bulkhead. Beside it, a cabin boy's hammock, still slung.
story.skycraft.q.pl_orphans_tear.o0.text: Recover the pay chest from the wreck
story.skycraft.q.pl_orphans_tear.o1.repl: Then they will be. I'll see to the list myself. And the boy, Tamsin? ...I'll write to Honorhall. Someone should.
story.skycraft.q.pl_orphans_tear.o1.text: Return the pay chest to the East Empire Company in Solitude
story.skycraft.q.pl_orphans_tear.o1.topi: The Orphan's Tear's pay chest. Her captain wanted the widows paid first.
story.skycraft.q.pl_orphans_tear.outro: The widows of the Orphan's Tear are paid in full that winter. The Company calls it a salvage fee. Aulus calls it an apology.
story.skycraft.q.pl_orphans_tear.pitch: The Orphan's Tear went down with eight hundred septims of Company pay aboard. Captain chained it to the bulkhead, so the story goes. Half the coast has tried for it. Mind the slaughterfish.
story.skycraft.q.pl_orphans_tear.title: Salvage Rights
story.skycraft.q.pl_pilgrims_trench.desc: Brother Aslaug of Windhelm drowned in Pilgrim's Trench carrying a relic arm-ring meant for Ysgramor's Tomb. His letter says it lies in an iron box under his bunk.
story.skycraft.q.pl_pilgrims_trench.o0.j: The arm-ring was still in its box, wrapped in a pilgrim's prayer cloth.
story.skycraft.q.pl_pilgrims_trench.o0.t: Find the iron box under Brother Aslaug's bunk
story.skycraft.q.pl_pilgrims_trench.o1.j: The arm-ring rests on the Harbinger's doorstep, as Brother Aslaug intended.
story.skycraft.q.pl_pilgrims_trench.o1.t: Lay the arm-ring at the door of Ysgramor's Tomb
story.skycraft.q.pl_pilgrims_trench.outr: Fishermen say that on the night you laid the ring, the wind off the trench sounded like many voices singing.
story.skycraft.q.pl_pilgrims_trench.pitc: Three pilgrim ships went down in the trench off the coast, carrying offerings for Ysgramor. One of them had a real Companion's arm-ring aboard, so the priests in Windhelm say.
story.skycraft.q.pl_pinefrost_tower.desc: Elenthir the exile hid a box of soul gems and coin at the foot of Pinefrost Tower: twelve paces downhill from the seaward side, under a flat grey stone with a hand-shaped lichen.
story.skycraft.q.pl_pinefrost_tower.o0.j: Under the stone, a small box: two charged soul gems and a purse of septims, and a note that just says 'Spite them well.'
story.skycraft.q.pl_pinefrost_tower.o0.t: Dig under the lichen-marked stone below Pinefrost Tower
story.skycraft.q.pl_pinefrost_tower.outr: The exile's reserve is yours. He asked only that it be spent on something the Thalmor would hate.
story.skycraft.q.pl_pinefrost_tower.pitc: That elf up at Rimerock left a stash somewhere near Pinefrost Tower, so the story goes. Under a stone with lichen like a hand. Spend it on something the Thalmor would hate, he said.
story.skycraft.q.pl_pinemoon_cave.desc: The Fort Hraggstad payroll was stolen on the Dragon Bridge road by bandits wearing pine sprigs. The quartermaster believes it went to Pinemoon Cave, where Rolf Coin-Biter holds court.
story.skycraft.q.pl_pinemoon_cave.o1.jou: Rolf kept the payroll strongbox under his bedroll, seal unbroken. He'd only bitten the lid.
story.skycraft.q.pl_pinemoon_cave.o2.jou: Quartermaster Calo counted it twice, then a third time, and then shook my hand for a very long while.
story.skycraft.q.pl_pinemoon_cave.o2.tex: Return the payroll to the quartermaster at Fort Hraggstad
story.skycraft.q.pl_pinemoon_cave.outro: The garrison at Fort Hraggstad gets paid for the first time in two months. Several soldiers stop talking about cousins in the Stormcloak camp.
story.skycraft.q.pl_pinemoon_cave.pitch: The Legion payroll got lifted on the Dragon Bridge road again. Pinemoon gang, wearing pine in their caps, bold as you like. The quartermaster at Hraggstad would kiss whoever brings that strongbox back.
story.skycraft.q.pl_pinemoon_cave.title: The Coin-Biter
